Question Choices: Point P is 3 units to the right of the origin and 5 units below it. Fill in the x-coordinate and then the y-coordinate.
Hints: Right of the origin means a positive x-coordinate.|Below the origin means a negative y-coordinate.
Solution: Moving 3 units right gives x = 3; moving 5 units below the origin gives y = -5. Write x first: (3, -5).

Question Choices: In which quadrant is the point (-4, 6)? Enter the quadrant number or Roman numeral.
Hints: A negative x-coordinate lies left of the y-axis.|A positive y-coordinate lies above the x-axis.
Solution: The x-coordinate is negative and the y-coordinate is positive: left of the y-axis and above the x-axis. These signs (-, +) identify Quadrant II.

Hints: Substitute -2 everywhere x appears.|Multiply before adding.
Solution: Substitute x = -2: 4x + 3 = 4(-2) + 3. Evaluate powers and products first. The signed terms are 3, -8; adding them gives -5.

Solution: Substitute a = 4 and b = -3: 3a - 2b = 3(4) - 2(-3). Evaluate powers and products first. The signed terms are 6, 12; adding them gives 18.

Question Choices: A rectangle has length x + 3 and width 4. What is its area when x = 5? Enter only the number.
Hints: Evaluate the length first.|Area equals length times width.
Solution: Substitute x = 5 into the length: 5 + 3 = 8. Area = length × width = 8 × 4 = 32 square units.
